note: CUT 65220 -> 58859 (-6,361, all in `harness`) by goal b5 step 2, the operator's decision of 2026-11-13 (R3379 -> R3383, his words: "Cut the bullets to conduct only - drop every field recital the enforced wire already carries", with "no field description is reworded" as part of the decision, not a caveat). 0.535.0 had already removed the ACTION SCHEMA dump wherever the wire enforces it; what remained was engine/kindprose.py's `Action kinds:` block, a THIRD copy of the same contract - the enforced wire carries every field description with its own words in front of the model, and step 1's field index carries the per-kind field map. Each of the 26 bullets keeps its IDENTITY clause - necessary, because ACTION_SCHEMA's `kind` is a BARE ENUM, so the wire says a kind exists and never what it is FOR - and keeps its CONDUCT, which exists nowhere else for a routine holding no corresponding rule (that is why the operator refused the option that moved conduct into rules). The field mechanics are gone. Not one field description was reworded. MEASURED, not estimated: the bullet table 23,853 -> 17,322 chars; through the real composer the harness section 29,805 -> 23,444. AN HONEST CORRECTION TO THE ESTIMATE GIVEN THE OPERATOR: he was told ~19k chars/turn; the real figure is -6,361, because the whole block had been counted as duplicate. Measured by 4-gram overlap against the 85 field descriptions the wire carries, only 2,416 of 23,853 chars overlapped at >=20%: the block was mostly identity and conduct, which this decision preserves. TWO CLAUSES WERE RESTORED after the first gate red (stamp 1794586344461292769-release) proved them CONTRACT rather than recital, which is the release gate working as designed: (1) the finish bullet's ok/partial/failed trichotomy, which D204 (operator, 2026-10-23) deliberately states on THREE surfaces at once - bullet, schema description and harness paragraph - so a run can never be told two different things about its own status, pinned by tests/test_partial_means_blocked.py; and (2) the memory bullet naming .memory/INDEX.md, pinned by tests/test_composer.py, the one place a run is told its notes are indexed. Both were re-added in their pinned core only; the elaborations around them really are on the wire verbatim and stayed cut. New pin tests/test_kind_bullets_carry_conduct.py holds the architecture: nine conduct sentences that must survive, and no bullet reciting field mechanics. `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately - this figure was locked with that command against the worktree's own src after the restoration, not before it. PREVIOUS: RAISED 64396 -> 65220 (+824, all in `schema`) for D268: `memory_write` gained `stale_after` and `verified`, a note's expiry and provenance as DATA (the operator's decided order, 2026-10-08: notes wrote 'verified live 2026-07-30' into their prose, where the one memory surface every run reads — the `.memory/` index in the state digest — could not read it). The cost is two field descriptions plus `verified`'s two sub-field descriptions, and they buy the three things a run cannot use the fields safely without: that `stale_after` is a DATE and not a duration; that past it the digest lists the note under its own heading rather than among the notes to consult (which is what makes setting it worth a run's attention); and that `verified.by` is `run` or `human:<who>`, since `human:operator` is what the operator's own confirmation renders as 'operator-verified'. The first draft cost +986 and was cut to this inside the same descriptions: 'for what you know will age' lost its justification clause, 'set it whenever you can name the date' went (the digest consequence already says it), and `by`/`at` dropped 'against the live thing' and 'it was checked'. Nothing was added to the harness — the mechanics (merge semantics, that an unrenderable value is left out rather than refused) live in engine/notemeta.py's docstring and in the memory_write OBSERVATION, which only a run that actually sets a field pays for. `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately: this is a hand edit measured with scheduler-builder's scripts/measure_prompt_budget against the worktree's own src, and the next CUT should lock itself in with that command. PREVIOUS: CUT 64397 -> 64396 (-1, all in `schema`) by D246 item (4): the `request` description said the user decides "once (this run) or forever" where `requests.DECISIONS` has THREE allow shapes — allow_now (this run), allow_once (ONE action), allow_forever — and allow_once is offered for exactly `entities.ONCE_CLASSES`, which is what a `request` takes. Naming the missing shape cost +10 and was paid back INSIDE the same description rather than by raising the ceiling ("denies, or allows it for this run, for ONE action, or forever" replaces "decides allow/deny, once (this run) or forever"; "applies it" replaces "applies the decision"; "names one" replaces "names an entity"). The release gate caught the +10 as a red in 0.514.0's first arming, which is the test working: measure with scheduler-builder's scripts/measure_prompt_budget BEFORE arming, since no targeted test run collects this file. PREVIOUS: CUT 64454 -> 64397 (-57: harness -66, schema +9) by WP4 (P3, a guard whose fix is mechanical applies it): the memory_write bullet and the content description no longer state a 100-line CAP (a note's size is advice now, engine/memops.py, so 'the cap is then measured against the RESULT' went with it), and the wait bullet names background landings in fewer words than the old any-exit sentence; the report `detail` and wait `all` descriptions grew to say a clipped tail is never re-filed and that `all` covers background calls. PREVIOUS: RAISED 64026 -> 64454 (+428, all in `schema`) for D231: the curator may dispose of a reminder row in ANOTHER routine's store (the operator's answer, 2026-11-02: "Give rules-review a way to delete/annotate a reminder row in a DISABLED routine's store (an engine capability or a census verb), since no report can reach a routine that never runs"). The cost is spread over four descriptions of the `remind` field and buys the three things a run cannot use the op safely without: that `op=dead` exists at all and is PREFERRED over `delete` (the operator's own ordering — `dead` keeps the row's hold tally, which is the evidence its pattern was too broad, and a deletion destroys exactly that); that `target` now means the disposal ops as well as `add`, so the row acted on is in ANOTHER routine's store; and that `description` carries the REASON on a disposal rather than a caution, since the reason is stored with the annotation and is required. The first draft cost +869 and was cut to this by removing the redundancy between the four clauses — the `target` description no longer restates what `dead` keeps, and the field summary says it in one clause instead of three sentences. Nothing was added to the harness: the dial, the refusal wording and the whole rationale live in docs/reminders.md and in the OBSERVATION `remind_write.curate` returns, which only a run that actually calls it pays for. `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately: this was a hand edit measured against the worktree's own src, and the next CUT should lock itself in with that command. PREVIOUS: RAISED 63670 -> 64026 (+356, all in `schema`) for D198: `create_routine` gained `revises`, the flag that REVISES an existing routine's recipe instead of creating one (the operator's answer, 2026-10-19: "Add a revise path to `create_routine` (or a sibling action) gated by a per-routine dial, like `config_confirm`"). The cost is one field description, and it is the only place a run learns the three things it cannot use the path safely without: that `prompt` carries the revision (one line per change, because the TARGET's run makes the edit from those words), that the target routine's own `revise_confirm` dial decides between a decision card and an immediate hand-over, and that the edit is made by that routine's next run and never by the caller — a run that believed it was writing another routine's files would propose a diff instead of prose, and a run not told the dial exists would re-issue a proposal that is already queued. Kept to a single clause: the dial's ladder, the proposer's capability and the refusal wording all live in the OBSERVATION the handler returns (engine/reviseroutine.py), which only a run that actually calls it pays for. No harness bullet was added — `create_routine`'s own bullet already names the kind, and a second always-on sentence about a mode most runs never use is what this budget exists to refuse. `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately: this was a hand edit, and the next CUT should lock itself in with that command. PREVIOUS: UNCHANGED 63670 by D227 (operator, 2026-10-31: 'Why not just remaining turns, minutes, tokens (if limited)?'), recorded here because the decision WAS about this budget and paid nothing into it. A run is now told what is left of its turns, minutes and (only when limited) tokens — but on the OBSERVATION TAIL (engine/loop._tails -> turnwindow.budget_left), not in the contract: this file measures `composer.system_sections`, which is composed ONCE at run start, so a number that changes every turn would be frozen at turn 1 and a lie on every later turn. Its cost is therefore bytes x TURNS in the messages array, where nothing ratchets it, so it is measured and pinned in tests/test_budget_left_line.py instead: 46 B/turn for the common run (turns + minutes, token budget unlimited), 75 B with a token ceiling, 91 B on a resumed leg — ~14 kB over a 300-turn run, against the 63670 chars this contract re-sends on every one of those same turns. '(if limited)' is enforced literally for that reason: an unlimited axis prints nothing rather than the word 'unlimited'. PREVIOUS: CUT 63712 -> 63670 (-42: harness -51, schema +9) by the Steward hub's retirement (operator, 2026-10-28): the finish summary now comes in two labelled parts, `**Process:**` (how the run went) then `**Work:**` (the task, its conditions and consequences), and the finish bullet names where decisions go instead of a page (a blocking ask when met, the rest batched before the finish). Paid for by the finish bullet no longer restating the schema's field list and by dropping the Markdown-rendering gloss (pipe tables, quotes) from both. PREVIOUS: CUT 63727 -> 63712 (-15, all in `schema`) by F787: the `questions` item schema's two decide-only sub-fields now lead with `decide ONLY:` so an ask_user batch is not offered a field askfields._DECIDE_ONLY refuses (folder-reorg:20261027-170451 turn 48 lost a turn to it), and the parent description stopped enumerating the per-question sub-fields the item schema already declares. The clarification is net-free: it pays for itself twice over. PREVIOUS: RAISED 62345 -> 63727 (+1382: +1008 `schema`, +374 `harness`) for D212 increment (a): one `ask_user` action may ask SEVERAL questions, and every filed decision record carries its CLASS. The cost is three things a run cannot use the feature without: the `questions` field's ask_user clause (the batch exists to be asked for), the new `blocks_work` field (the class override, whose description has to state the test it claims — `without this answer the run cannot do the work it was fired to do` — AND that it is not `mode`, because confusing the recorded class with the waiting mode is the one misreading that would make a run park itself), and the harness bullet that tells a run the batch exists at all. The first draft cost +2667; it was cut to this by dropping the justification prose from the bullet, shortening both clauses, and leaving the per-question sub-fields declared but undescribed (they mean for their question exactly what the same-named top-level field means, the way decide's items are already undescribed). What it buys back is measured, on the asking side rather than the contract: 37% of runs (60 of 163 over 282 real question records) already asked more than one question, up to 6, one action and one turn each, at a median 430 tokens of question prose per ask — so a run that batches 3 asks saves 2 turns of its own context, which is larger than 1382 chars, and the operator gets one grouped card set instead of 3 unrelated ones (51% of his answering sittings already disposed of several at once). `python tests/test_prompt_budget.py --update` refuses to raise, deliberately: this was a hand edit, and the next CUT should lock itself in with that command. PREVIOUS: RAISED 61821 -> 62345 (+524, all in `schema`) for D118 phase 3: the `background` field's description is the only place a run learns WHICH kinds may be deferred and what the ordering promise is, and phase 3 made three mutations deferrable behind a dependency barrier (engine/background_order.py). A run that is not told a write may defer, that touching the declared target is held until it lands, that a second deferred write to one target is refused and that a `then_script` may not ride a deferred change cannot use the feature safely — and the previous wording actively forbade it (`NOT available on a WRITING KIND`), so the engine accepted what every model was told to refuse.
